prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate change to a 3D-IC physical design flow.
Hypothesis of the change: The parent (c007) enables timing-driven net weighting but relies on the default `momentum_decay_factor` for the Adam-style criticality momentum; lowering it makes the criticality signal track the *current* placement more responsively each iteration, so many moderately-critical nets keep meaningful weight instead of being dominated by a few early-identified critical nets — spreading buffer-friendly weight across more violating paths and reducing TNS.
Rule-based digest:
total=+0.453 robust(mean-std)=+0.098 min_case=+0.077 all_valid=True
  ariane133-ng45: score=+0.200 dWNS=+10.8% dTNS=+25.9% overflow~90
  bp-ng45: score=+0.077 dWNS=+11.7% dTNS=+4.9% overflow~104
  bp_fe-ng45: score=+0.176 dWNS=+15.6% dTNS=+18.9% overflow~127
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: The hypothesis held: all three cases improved, with dWNS +10.8–15.6% and dTNS +4.9–25.9%, robust score +0.098 and min_case +0.077. The mechanism fits—lower momentum decay lets criticality track current placement, spreading weight to moderately-critical nets rather than a few early nets, reducing TNS (largest gain on ariane133, +25.9%). Overflow ~90–127 suggests routing pressure worth watching. Next step: sweep `momentum_decay_factor` across a small grid (e.g., 0.5×, 0.25× default) on these cases to confirm monotonic benefit and check overflow/routability doesn't degrade.
